findings.lens: charismatic non-denominational (Vineyard, Bethel, Hillsong, Third Wave)
findings.claim: 'fulfilled literally in a future earthly kingdom' fuses two questions (does ethnic Israel have a future? is there an earthly millennium?) in dispensational vocabulary ('literally').
findings.evidence: A historic premillennialist (Ladd, Vineyard) affirms a future earthly reign but denies a separate program for national Israel; a Romans-11 pro-Israel charismatic (Bethel, IHOP, Hillsong) affirms a future for Israel but not 'literally' in the Ryrie sense. Both are forced to guess which clause the scorer means. AoG Fundamental Truth 14 ('the salvation of national Israel') shows this is the classical Pentecostal wording, which is fine, but the axis is supposed to separate that view from mine.
findings.fix: 'God still has a distinct future plan for ethnic Israel that is not simply absorbed into the church.'

findings.claim: "fulfilled literally" is our own vocabulary, and the other side will read it as implying they do not interpret literally.
findings.evidence: Riddlebarger, A Case for Amillennialism (2003; cited in the read-more) argues at length that amillennialists interpret 'literally' according to genre; Horton makes the same point. Dispensationalists can answer the item honestly, but the fairness promise covers both sides.
findings.fix: "God still has a distinct future for national Israel: the land and kingdom promises will be fulfilled for ethnic Israel in an earthly kingdom after Christ returns." (direction +1).

findings.lens: Reformed charismatic (John Piper, Wayne Grudem, Sam Storms, Sovereign Grace Churches, Acts 29 continuationists)
findings.claim: 'God's promises to national Israel will be fulfilled literally in a future earthly kingdom' is double-barreled: Israel/church distinction plus a future earthly kingdom, and historic premillennialists hold the second without the first.
findings.evidence: Piper, Grudem (Systematic Theology ch. 55) and Ladd, whom this axis's own history cites at 1950s, expect an earthly millennial reign of Christ and a future conversion of ethnic Israel (Rom 11:26) while denying a separate national program; they cannot answer without conceding a dispensational distinctive they reject. The Israel/church question is already covered by statement 11.
findings.fix: Old Testament promises to Israel (land, throne, temple) must be fulfilled literally to ethnic Israel, not fulfilled in Christ and the church.

findings.claim: "fulfilled literally" is dispensationalist self-description; covenantal readers claim they also read literally according to genre, and Reformed readers who expect a future calling of the Jews half-agree with "promises to national Israel will be fulfilled".
findings.evidence: Ryrie, Dispensationalism, makes "consistent literal interpretation" the sine qua non; Westminster Larger Catechism Q.191 prays that "the Jews [be] called". The direction (+1) is correct.
findings.fix: Replace with: "God will yet give the nation of Israel its promised land and kingdom on this earth." (16 words, direction +1).
